title: Congestion isolation: shard reservoirs with soft rollback
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Problem: During cross-tenant spikes we observe noisy-neighbor congestion that causes tail latency for small, latency-sensitive requests. Existing global token-bucket shedding is too coarse — it leads to large blast radiuses and unstable failovers across regions. Goal: implement a congestion-isolation pattern using per-shard reservoirs that deterministically split resident capacity between tenants and request classes, provide graceful degradation hooks and a soft rollback to retry or route to degraded responses when possible, and integrate with circuit breakers and multi-region failover policies.
acceptance_criteria: Per-shard reservoir allocator exists and can be configured via the runtime config with weights and min-fair-share
Deterministic dropping implemented (hash-based) so two retries from same client follow same decision path until state changes
When a request is dropped we emit structured telemetry: drop_reason, shard_id, tenant_id, decision_version
Soft rollback policy will attempt 1 degraded fallback (model-variant or truncation) or route to companion region within 200ms when configured
End-to-end tests show p99 tail latency for latency-sensitive class improves by >=15% under a synthetic noisy-tenant spike
Canary rollout plan documented and automated feature flag exists to toggle per-shard mode
Runbook pages updated with 'how to diagnose' and 'how to escalate' steps
design_notes: We split the serving fleet into logical shards (existing shard_id used for KV & routing). Each shard maintains a reservoir token pool updated every second based on configured throughput and active tenant weights.

Deterministic dropping: requests are assigned a deterministic sample id (sha256(tenant_id + request_hash + decision_epoch) mod reservoir_size) so the same request pattern maps consistently while epoch is stable. This reduces flapping across retries.

Soft rollback options: 1) fallback model variant (smaller model/quantized); 2) truncated response pipeline (prefix-only); 3) region fallback to paired read-only region. The runtime will try fallbacks in configured order until an SLA path succeeds or budget exhausted.

Circuit-breaker interaction: per-shard circuit has three levels (healthy, degraded, tripped). Tripped shards mark all non-critical classes for immediate reservoir rejection. Health transitions are based on sliding-window error/latency budgets tied to SLOs.
implementation_steps: 1) Add reservoir state machine to runtime shard manager with config knobs: base_capacity, tenant_weight_map, min_reserve
2) Implement deterministic sampling util and hook into admission path path just before enqueueing into batcher
3) Expose SDK/REST headers for clients to opt-in to deterministic retry semantics (for idempotent requests)
4) Implement soft rollback orchestrator that can trigger model-variant or truncated-response handlers
5) Wire circuit-breaker signals into shard reservoir to flip into tripped mode under sustained latency/exceptions
6) Emit structured telemetry to metrics pipeline and add logs for initial debug build
7) Add feature flag and runtime config delta to allow progressive rollout
8) End-to-end load testing and chaos scenarios (node failure, cross-region latency, tenant spike)
rollout_plan: Dev environment: unit tests + integration tests (local shards) - done
Staging: enable feature flag for 5% of shards, run synthetic noisy-tenant and golden path workloads - target date 2026-03-10
Canary: ramp to 20% shards in us-west with active customers flagged; monitor reservoir metrics, drop_reason ratios, rollback_success_rate - 72h observation
Progressive: 50% then 100% after SLA checks and postmortem of canary anomalies
Fallback: feature flag off + global circuit-breaker forced degrade if we see regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests for deterministic sampler, reservoir accounting, and rollback orchestration
Integration test that simulates retries and verifies deterministic decisions across epochs
Load test: recreate noisy-tenant pattern (80% of tokens from synthetic tenant) and measure p50/p95/p99 for latency-sensitive class
Chaos test: introduce 250ms cross-region latency and verify failover path triggers and respects SLA budget
SLO regression harness: run nightly job comparing baseline and new behavior across 14-day windows
notes: Design tradeoff: deterministic dropping reduces variance on retries but can introduce correlated drops for bursty tenants; mitigated by decision_epoch rotation and tenant_weight smoothing.
We must reconcile reservoir accounting with existing KV cache fastpath to avoid double-accounting for very short-circuit requests.
Coordination: engage SE for top customers before canary to communicate potential degraded modes and region-fallback behavior.
Follow-ups: explore automatic tenant re-weighting based on historical consumption and business priority mappings (PM to scope).
